Who We Are

We are a research and engineering group focused on the intersection of autonomous systems, formal governance, and applied cybernetics. At CyberAlchemy AI, we build architectures designed to understand and steer complex environments.

What We Believe

We believe that research is fundamentally a method for discovering and mapping unknown domains. In this paradigm, any software constructed is just a tool for this discovery.

Code is not the end product. It is an observational probe we send into a domain to chart its territory, measure its dynamics, and return empirical evidence.

How We Work: Cybernetics Squared

Because we harness and research cybernetic theory, we apply those principles to the very tools we build. We engineer systems that act as cybernetic loops to human economic activity: tracking intent, interpreting reality, verifying alignment, and feeding data back to human operators.

Project Saturn: Continuous Cybernetic Alignment

Software projects begin with a blueprint. But once deployed, decay begins. The system in production diverges from the system on paper. Specifications rot, governance becomes a suggestion, and telemetry throws dashboards at us without offering control.

The force pulling intent and reality apart is drift. Traditional engineering treats design and operation as a one-way street: we build it, we ship it, and we watch it. Without a feedback loop, divergence is inevitable.

Closing the Loop

Project Saturn was born from one question: What if a system could defend its own architecture?

Saturn treats domain intent as a reference baseline. By measuring reality against this baseline, Saturn does not only report drift, it acts on it, turning governance into executable behavior.

The Architecture of Convergence

Saturn operates as a lifecycle: observe telemetry, evaluate against contracts, decide corrective states, execute routing, and verify closure. Intent flows downward into execution, and truth flows upward to inform governance.

Saturn traverses every layer as a meta-loop: reading telemetry from perception layers, evaluating it against intent layers, and triggering responses through execution and regulation layers.

Without this kind of loop, teams rely on heroics to keep systems aligned. Saturn transforms telemetry into sensory input for a governance engine, enabling deterministic self-correction.

Project MARS

MARS is the research orchestration project that defines and validates a gated, reproducible lifecycle for experiment design, execution, evidence adjudication, and paper integration.

Core Question

Can we run research programs with deterministic governance gates, explicit dependency contracts, and traceable evidence updates so that claim quality improves over time?

Canonical Asset Model

To ensure rigor, MARS uses canonical reusable definitions and templates. Research is organized into executable phases, extracting high-fidelity data that maps unknown edges of agentic systems.

Project MOGT: Multi-Objective Game Theory

This project tests whether multi-objective game theory can improve how agentic systems make conversation-level decisions while balancing competing forces.

Core Hypothesis

Can explicit multi-objective and game-theoretic decision policies outperform implicit heuristic arbitration in agentic conversations when optimizing for quality, cost, latency, safety, and escalation risk?

Primary Concerns

  • Whether explicit objective vectors improve traceability of agent decisions.
  • Whether Pareto-aware selection improves outcome quality under competing goals.
  • Whether negotiation and equilibrium-inspired coordination reduce unresolved disagreement.
